ORIG-COM.ref_text: I think the idea of capturing the global structure with a VAE and modeling the local structure with a PixelCNN decoder makes a lot of sense and can prevent the blurry reconstruction/samples of VAE. I specially like the hierarchical image generation experiments.
ORIG-COM.test_text: - ORIG: The paper presents a compelling and well-articulated combination of VAEs and PixelCNNs, leveraging the complementary strengths of both architectures to address their respective limitations. Evidence anchors: SRC-001, SRC-002, SRC-005.

QUAL-CMP.ref_text: 2) A similar idea is also presented in a concurrent ICLR submission "Variational Lossy Autoencoder". It would be interesting to have a discussion included in the paper and compare these works.
QUAL-CMP.test_text:
- QUAL: The comparison on 64x64 ImageNet is limited to PixelRNN and Gated PixelCNN, missing comparisons to other relevant state-of-the-art generative models available at the time. Evidence anchors: SRC-011.

- Suggested revision for QUAL opinion 4: Expand the baseline comparisons on 64x64 ImageNet to include other recent state-of-the-art models to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of the model's performance.

QUAL-EXP.ref_text:
4) As pointed out in my pre-review question, it would be great to include two sets of MNIST samples maybe in an appendix section. One with PixelCNN and the other with PixelVAE with the same pixelcnn depth to illustrate the hidden code in PixelVAE actually captures the global structure.

On the experimental side, I would have liked to see something more than NLL measurements and samples - maybe show this is useful for other tasks such as classification?

1) Is there any experiment showing that using the PixelCNN as the decoder of VAE will result in better disentangling of high-level factors of variations in the hidden code?
For example, the authors can train a PixelVAE and VAE on MNIST with 2D hidden code and visualize the 2D hidden code for test images and color code each hidden code based on the digit and show that the digits have a better separation in the PixelVAE representation. A semi-supervised classification comparison between VAE and the PixelVAE will also significantly improve the quality of the paper.
QUAL-EXP.test_text:
- QUAL: The experimental evaluation on the LSUN bedrooms dataset lacks quantitative metrics such as log-likelihood or FID, relying solely on qualitative sample inspection and vague claims of outperforming baselines. Evidence anchors: SRC-010.

- Suggested revision for QUAL opinion 2: Provide quantitative log-likelihood or other standard metrics for the LSUN bedrooms experiments to objectively validate the claim that the model outperforms the two-level convolutional VAE and single-level PixelVAE.

- ORIG: The experimental setup includes a novel ablation study on the number of PixelCNN layers, showing that PixelVAE achieves strong performance with significantly fewer autoregressive layers than PixelCNN, highlighting an important efficiency advantage. Evidence anchors: SRC-007, SRC-008.

QUAL-MET.ref_text: I think the model is quite clever, attempting to get the best of latent variable models and auto-regressive models. The implementation and specific architecture choices (as discussed in the pre-review) also seem reasonable.
QUAL-MET.test_text: - QUAL: The proposed model architecture is technically sound, correctly formulating the VAE objective with an autoregressive decoder and providing a clear derivation for the hierarchical extension. Evidence anchors: SRC-005, SRC-006.

QUAL-REP.ref_text: 3) The answer to the pre-review questions made the architecture details of the paper much more clear, but I still ask the authors to include the exact architecture details of all the experiments in the paper and/or open source the code. The clarity of the presentation is not satisfying and the experiments are difficult to reproduce.
QUAL-REP.test_text:
- QUAL: The paper lacks sufficient implementation details for reproducibility, omitting specific hyperparameters such as learning rates, batch sizes, and exact layer dimensions, and does not provide code availability. Evidence anchors: SRC-007, SRC-011.

- Suggested revision for QUAL opinion 3: Include a detailed appendix with all hyperparameters, network architecture specifications, and training protocols, and make the code publicly available to facilitate reproduction.
